title: X Minus One
paragraphs: NBC's classic science-fiction anthology adapted stories by major genre writers and presented original scripts about space, aliens, future societies, technology, and the social consequences of scientific change.

Adult science-fiction anthology continuing the creative line of Dimension X. Frozen GRH snapshot contains 121 objects from the 1955-58 original run plus the 1973 experimental revival, so it does not represent all 126 original-run broadcasts.

GRH documents the program through NBC original run (April 24, 1955 to January 9, 1958) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and 1973 experimental revival (January 27, 1973 to January 27, 1973).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are William Welch (producer on 113 recordings and radio adaptor on 6 recordings), Fred Collins (announcer on 106 recordings), Daniel Sutter (director on 71 recordings and transcriber on 7 recordings), Ernest Kinoy (radio adaptor on 56 recordings and writer on 9 recordings), George Lefferts (radio adaptor on 38 recordings, writer on 9 recordings, and author on 1 recording), Bob Hastings (performer on 34 recordings), and Wendell Holmes (performer on 26 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]] (originated at station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include space travel and exploration, time travel and temporal displacement, alien life and first contact, human identity and personhood, robots and artificial beings, and computers and artificial intelligence.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Dimension X predecessor and script continuity, Science-fiction magazine adaptation pipeline, Adult science fiction in network radio’s television era, and Old-time-radio nostalgia revival attempt.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (73 shared credited people), [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] (64 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (68 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (62 shared credited people), and [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (60 shared credited people).
